what: The LCM and HCF Calculator finds the lowest common multiple and the highest common factor (also called GCD or GCF) of two or more whole numbers, and shows the working in two ways: prime factorization and Euclid's division method.

Below it, a prime checker tells you whether a number is prime, gives its prime factorization and number of divisors, and finds the previous and next prime. It is made for homework, revision and checking answers.
uses: Check LCM and HCF answers with the full working.
Find the lowest common denominator for adding fractions.
Find when repeating events line up again (LCM).
Find the largest equal size that fits (HCF).
Test whether numbers are prime and factor them.
tutorial: Enter two or more whole numbers separated by commas or spaces.
The HCF and LCM appear at the top.
Each number is written as a product of primes; HCF takes the smallest powers and LCM the largest.
Each division step a = q × b + r is listed until the remainder is 0.
Type a number in the prime checker to see if it is prime and its factors.
Press "Copy answer and steps" to paste them into your notes.
features: LCMs of any size are calculated exactly.
Tells you when the numbers share no factor.
Factorization, divisor count, previous and next prime.

example.title: Worked example: 12, 18 and 30
example.text: 12 = 2² × 3, 18 = 2 × 3² and 30 = 2 × 3 × 5. The HCF takes the common primes with the smallest powers: 2 × 3 = 6. The LCM takes every prime with the largest power: 2² × 3² × 5 = 180.

tips: HCF × LCM = a × b for two numbers, a quick way to check.
If one number divides the others, it is the HCF.
Use the LCM of denominators to add fractions.
problems: Every number divides 0, so LCM and HCF with 0 are not useful. Remove it.
It says the number is not a whole number
Use whole numbers only, without decimals or minus signs.
Numbers above one trillion are only solved with Euclid's method to keep it fast.
